President Donald Trump’s approval rating dropped to the lowest level of his second term in the White House.

In a new Reuters/Ipsos poll, only 33% of Americans in the survey admitted that they approved of Trump's performance in the White House, while 64% disapproved.

results.title: Trump's approval rating falls to new low in latest poll

results.content:
Just 33% of respondents in the four-day survey said they approved of Trump's performance in the White House, while 64% disapproved. Trump's approval rating, down from 35% in a poll that closed earlier this month and ​lower than at any point in his current term, has now tied the lowest level of his prior term reached in December 2017.

Aug. 16Trump had a 35% approval rating and 55% disapproval rating in a Financial Times/Focaldata poll of 1,913 registered voters conducted Aug. 7-10 (margin of error 2.9).

Trump’s net approval rating among Republicans has dropped eight points since the groups’ survey last month, the Financial Times reported.

The poll comes as inflation cooled in July from June, but at 3.4%, it’s still higher than when Trump took office as the war with Iran has driven up fuel costs and disrupted the economy. [...] Meanwhile, Democrats have a five percentage-point advantage over Republicans in the upcoming midterm elections, according to the survey.
